subject: GreenStream POC sprint plan, success criteria, and risk triage
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@greenstream.ai>
Cc: GreenStream Procurement <procurement@greenstream.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: GreenStream POC — proposed sprint plan & success criteria

Hi Olivia — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and a proposed 4-week POC sprint plan so we can align on success criteria, owners, and timeline. Please review and confirm or call out edits.

Recap (from discovery):
- Goal: Validate Redwood can serve Gen-2 summarization + semantic search at GreenStream scale and latency targets while meeting data controls.
- Top priority: predictable p50 latency, embedding accuracy on their ranked test set, and operational observability.

Proposed POC success criteria (compact):
1) Latency: p50 generation <= 300ms for 1k token context on configured instance profile.
2) Throughput: support 10 concurrent workers with <5% error rate at target batching policy.
3) Embedding quality: ≥0.85 top-5 MAP on GreenStream test queries (we will run the dataset you shared).
4) Data controls: VPC egress locked, audit logs visible in console for all requests during POC.

High-level sprint plan (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): Exchange access, SOW + procurement, security questionnaire.
- Week 1: Env & infra setup, baseline smoke tests, connectivity validation.
- Week 2: Integration + sample throughput tests; collect evaluation outputs.
- Week 3: Tune quantization/batching, run eval harness, measure quality metrics.
- Week 4: Final analysis, sign-off decision, optional extension or handoff.

Owners (Redwood):
- AE / PM: Ben Carter (me) — commercial lead
- SE: Lauren Bishop — integration & performance tuning
- CS: Monica Patel — acceptance, runbooks, handoff

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_stub_v1.pdf (SOW stub), integration-preflight-checklist.xlsx
Links: evaluation folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-greenstream-poc)

Ask: Can you confirm the success criteria above and procurement timing (target sign by 2027-04-07)? Also confirm kickoff availability (proposed Apr 6).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-04T08:45:00Z
Subject: Internal: preflight finding — long-context tokenization incompatibility (action + escalation)

Internal note (please do not forward to GreenStream yet). During prep with the sample bundle GreenStream shared, I ran the tokenization/ingestion pipeline and observed a repeatable condition: their pre-tokenized documents occasionally produce sequence lengths > 32k tokens (their chunking is document-based, not token-aware). Redwood’s current runtime variant we planned to use caps context handling at 32k tokens for prefix caching; at scale this causes a runtime OOM on our current batch policy during prefix/KV caching.

Impact: failing smoke tests when running realistic batch sizes; could block Week 1 integration and push evaluation back.

Mitigation options (short-term):
- Option A (recommended immediate): Force chunked-streaming calls on those long documents (client-side chunking with sequence overlap 256 tokens). This requires a small change to their ingestion flow but no infra code changes.
- Option B (fallback): Use quantized model variant with smaller KV memory usage — reduces accuracy slightly but avoids OOM.
- Option C (runtime fix): Increase runtime KV capacity and adjust batching heuristics (requires a runtime deployment and may take 48–72 hrs).

Proposed escalation path:
1) Lauren implements Option A as a stop-gap and documents steps (owned by me).
2) Rishi to open a runtime incident and tag INF-1029 to evaluate whether we can get a hotfix / temporarily raise KV caps for this customer.
3) Monica to coordinate messaging and updated timelines to GreenStream if runtime fix needed.

I will prepare a short risk-log CSV and include example failing records. If we can get procurement + GreenStream to accept client-side chunking for POC, we can keep the April 6 kickoff and compress Week 1 troubleshooting.

-Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-04T10:00:00Z
Subject: GreenStream POC — small pre-kickoff update and ask on long-context docs

Olivia / procurement — quick transparency note ahead of kickoff. Our SE team discovered a preflight compatibility issue with a subset of your documents that produce tokenized sequences > 32k. This can cause OOMs in our planned runtime configuration when running larger, realistic batch sizes.

Planned mitigation / asks:
- Short-term: We can proceed with the POC if GreenStream is comfortable with client-side chunking for these long docs (we recommend overlap=256 tokens). This is the fastest path and keeps the April 6 kickoff intact.
- If chunking is not acceptable, we will: (a) enable the quantized model variant as a fallback (minor quality impact) or (b) initiate runtime hotfix (JIRA INF-1029) which could add 48–72 hours to week-0 activities.

Attachments: greenstream-poc-risk-log.csv (sample failing records + suggested chunking script snippet)
Links: JIRA-INF-1029, https://docs.docusign.net/s/ABC-POC-SOW

Ask for GreenStream: please confirm whether client-side chunking is acceptable for the POC, or whether you require full long-document preservation (in which case we will scope the runtime fix and adjust the kickoff timeline).

We propose keeping the Apr 6 kickoff but adding a 30–45 minute slot for runtime triage and next-step decisions. Ben will send updated agenda.

Thanks — Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
